elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added clause requires Vendor to “defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates” from third-party claims alleging that the Services or any Deliverable infringes or misappropriates an intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) expressly covers third-party claims arising from “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, which operatively addresses a Vendor-caused data breach.

elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) expressly covers “Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the indemnified party to notify the indemnifying party of the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party notice of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defence.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the indemnifying Party shall control the defence.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the indemnified party to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The clause requires the indemnified Party to provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity may cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity may cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must not extend beyond claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The former indemnity for every claim relating to Customer's use is replaced with an exhaustive scope limited to third-party claims arising from the two permitted categories.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added Vendor indemnity expressly covers third-party IP infringement and misappropriation claims involving the Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Customer appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications or instructions.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Customer specifications or instructions appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor must have an IP-infringement remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No operative procurement remedy is included. Section 9.3 merely references remedies allegedly required by Section 20.5, but no such remedy language is present in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor must have an IP-infringement remedy to modify the affected Services or Deliverables so they become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No operative modification remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor must have an IP-infringement remedy to replace the affected Services or Deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: No operative replacement remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a refund if the other IP-infringement remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: No operative refund remedy or associated trigger appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no indemnity cap or reference to a cap equal to three times annual fees.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position by adding the required Vendor indemnities, correctly directing notice/control/cooperation obligations, and narrowing Customer's indemnity to the two permitted categories. It does not satisfy the fallback because the usual IP exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The changes are confined to the requested indemnity allocation and leave unrelated commercial terms effective. Drafting quality is reduced by the dangling reference to Section 20.5 and the absence of customary procedural details such as prompt notice, prejudice protection, cooperation expenses, and settlement restrictions.
